requirements.text: Upon loading the Tic Tac Toe webpage, the system must display the following UI elements: a title with the text 'Tic Tac Toe', a message indicating the current player's turn ('Player X's turn') within an element identified by the attribute data-testid='current-player', a 3x3 grid of tiles each uniquely identified by data-testid attributes ranging from 'tile-1' to 'tile-9', and a reset button identified by data-testid='reset-button'. All tiles must initially be empty, without any inner text or classes 'playerX' or 'playerO'.

When a player clicks on an empty tile, the system must display the current player's symbol ('X' or 'O') in the tile and visually indicate the player's move by adding a corresponding CSS class ('playerX' for Player X or 'playerO' for Player O). The system must validate that the tile is empty before allowing the action. If the tile is already occupied, no changes should be made to the tile's content or CSS class, and the current player should remain unchanged. The tiles are identified using the 'data-testid' attribute (e.g., 'tile-1', 'tile-2', etc.). The current player's symbol is displayed in the element with 'data-testid="current-player"', and its CSS class dynamically updates to reflect the active player ('playerX' or 'playerO').

When a player clicks on a tile that is already occupied, the system must ignore the action and prevent any changes to the tile or game state. Specifically: 1) The tile's content (innerText) and associated class (e.g., 'playerX' or 'playerO') must remain unchanged. 2) The current player indicator (element with data-testid='current-player') must not update. 3) The game state must remain active or inactive as it was prior to the click. 4) If the game is inactive (e.g., after a win or tie), clicking on any tile must not alter the announcer's message (element with data-testid='announcer') or the game state. These behaviors must apply consistently across all tiles (elements with class 'tile' and data-testid attributes 'tile-1' through 'tile-9').

When a player wins the Tic Tac Toe game, the system must display a message in the announcer section indicating the winner ('Player X Won' or 'Player O Won') and prevent further interactions with the game board. Specifically: 1) The announcer section (identified by the attribute data-testid='announcer') must display the text 'Player X Won' or 'Player O Won' based on the winning player, with the winner's symbol styled using the respective CSS class ('playerX' or 'playerO'). 2) The announcer section must have the 'hide' class removed to make it visible. 3) All tiles on the game board (identified by the class 'tile' and data-testid attributes such as 'tile-1', 'tile-2', etc.) must no longer accept user clicks or updates. This behavior must apply to all winning scenarios, including normal cases, edge cases (e.g., winning on the last move), and boundary conditions (e.g., winning with the minimum number of moves).

When the game ends in a tie (i.e., all tiles are filled without any player meeting the winning conditions), the system must perform the following actions: 1) Display the message 'Tie' in the announcer section, replacing its innerText with 'Tie'. 2) Ensure the announcer section becomes visible by removing the 'hide' class from its class list. 3) Disable further interactions with the game board by preventing any additional clicks on tiles. The announcer section is identified by the attribute 'data-testid="announcer"', and each tile on the game board is identified by the attribute 'data-testid' with values ranging from 'tile-1' to 'tile-9'.

Upon loading the Tic Tac Toe game, the system initializes with Player X as the current player, indicated by the player display element with data-testid 'current-player'. The game board consists of nine tiles, each with a unique data-testid ranging from 'tile-1' to 'tile-9'. When a user clicks on a tile, if the tile is empty and the game is active, the system updates the tile to display the current player's symbol ('X' or 'O') and adds a corresponding class ('playerX' or 'playerO'). Subsequently, the system switches the current player, updating the player display element to reflect the new player's turn ('Player X's turn' or 'Player O's turn'). This change is visually represented by updating the inner text and class of the player display element. The system ensures that the player switch only occurs after a valid move, maintaining the integrity of the game flow.

When the reset button (with data-testid 'reset-button') is clicked, the system must perform the following actions: clear all tiles (elements with data-testid 'tile-1' to 'tile-9'), reset the internal game board state to all empty values, hide the announcer section (element with data-testid 'announcer'), and set the current player to 'X' in the element with data-testid 'current-player' if it was previously 'O'. This functionality should work correctly in various scenarios, including when some tiles are marked, when the game is in progress, when a win has been announced, when a tie has been announced, and when no tiles have been marked.

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Verify the page displays all required elements on load
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display initial game state on page load
  The system must display the correct UI elements when the page loads, including a 3x3 grid of tiles, a title, a message indicating the current player's turn, and a reset button.


  Scenario: [Normal] Verify the page displays all required elements on load
    Given the user opens the Tic Tac Toe webpage
    Then the page should display a title with the text "Tic Tac Toe"
    And the page should display a message indicating "Player X's turn" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
    And the page should display a 3x3 grid of tiles, each with a data-testid from "tile-1" to "tile-9"
    And the page should display a reset button with data-testid "reset-button"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Verify the page loads correctly with no pre-filled tiles
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display initial game state on page load
  The system must display the correct UI elements when the page loads, including a 3x3 grid of tiles, a title, a message indicating the current player's turn, and a reset button.


  Scenario: [Edge] Verify the page loads correctly with no pre-filled tiles
    Given the user opens the Tic Tac Toe webpage
    Then each tile with data-testid from "tile-1" to "tile-9" should be empty
    And no tile should have a class of "playerX" or "playerO"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player X clicks on an empty tile
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display current player's symbol on tile click
  The system must display the current player's symbol ('X' or 'O') in the clicked tile and visually indicate the player's move by adding a corresponding CSS class.


  Scenario: [Normal] Player X clicks on an empty tile
    Given the Tic Tac Toe webpage is loaded
    And the current player is displayed as "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
    When the player clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should display "X"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should have the CSS class "playerX"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player O clicks on an empty tile
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display current player's symbol on tile click
  The system must display the current player's symbol ('X' or 'O') in the clicked tile and visually indicate the player's move by adding a corresponding CSS class.


Scenario: [Normal] Player O clicks on an empty tile
    Given the Tic Tac Toe webpage is loaded
    And the player clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    And the current player is displayed as "O" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
    When the player clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-2"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-2" should display "O"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-2" should have the CSS class "playerO"

reference_cases.title: [Error] Player clicks on a tile that is already occupied
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display current player's symbol on tile click
  The system must display the current player's symbol ('X' or 'O') in the clicked tile and visually indicate the player's move by adding a corresponding CSS class.


  Scenario: [Error] Player clicks on a tile that is already occupied
    Given the Tic Tac Toe webpage is loaded
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-5" displays "X"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-5" has the CSS class "playerX"
    And the current player is displayed as "O" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
    When the player clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-5"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-5" should still display "X"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-5" should still have the CSS class "playerX"
    And the current player should still be displayed as "O" in the element with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player clicks on an unoccupied tile
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Prevent changes when clicking on an occupied tile
  The system must ignore any action when a player clicks on a tile that is already occupied, ensuring no changes to the tile or game state.


  Scenario: [Normal] Player clicks on an unoccupied tile
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the current player is "X"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should display "X"
    And the current player should be "O"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player clicks on an occupied tile
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Prevent changes when clicking on an occupied tile
  The system must ignore any action when a player clicks on a tile that is already occupied, ensuring no changes to the tile or game state.


  Scenario: [Normal] Player clicks on an occupied tile
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-1" displays "X"
    And the current player is "O"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should still display "X"
    And the current player should remain "O"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Player clicks on multiple occupied tiles consecutively
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Prevent changes when clicking on an occupied tile
  The system must ignore any action when a player clicks on a tile that is already occupied, ensuring no changes to the tile or game state.


  Scenario: [Edge] Player clicks on multiple occupied tiles consecutively
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-1" displays "X"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-2" displays "O"
    And the current player is "X"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    And the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-2"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should still display "X"
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-2" should still display "O"
    And the current player should remain "X"

reference_cases.title: [Error] Player attempts to click on an occupied tile after game is won
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Prevent changes when clicking on an occupied tile
  The system must ignore any action when a player clicks on a tile that is already occupied, ensuring no changes to the tile or game state.


Scenario: [Error] Player attempts to click on an occupied tile after game is won
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the tiles with data-testids "tile-1", "tile-2", and "tile-3" display "X", and data-testids "tile-4" and "tile-5" display "O"
    And the announcer displays "Player X Won"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should still display "X"
    And the announcer should still display "Player X Won"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player X wins the game
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display Winner Announcement and Stop Further Interactions
  The system must display a message indicating the winner and stop further interactions with the game board when a player wins.


  Scenario: [Normal] Player X wins the game
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
    And the tiles with data-testids "tile-1" and "tile-2" display "X", and "tile-4" and "tile-5" display "O"
    And the current player is "X"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-3"
    Then the announcer section should display "Player X Won"
    And the announcer section should not have the class "hide"
    And all tiles on the game board should no longer accept clicks

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player O wins the game
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display Winner Announcement and Stop Further Interactions
  The system must display a message indicating the winner and stop further interactions with the game board when a player wins.


Scenario: [Normal] Player O wins the game
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
    And the tiles with data-testids "tile-4", "tile-5", and "tile-7" display "X", and "tile-1" and "tile-2" display "O"
    And the current player is "O"
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-3"
    Then the announcer section should display "Player O Won"
    And the announcer section should not have the class "hide"
    And all tiles on the game board should no longer accept clicks

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Winning condition on the last move
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display Winner Announcement and Stop Further Interactions
  The system must display a message indicating the winner and stop further interactions with the game board when a player wins.


Scenario: [Edge] Winning condition on the last move
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
    And the current player is "X"
    And the board state is ["X", "X", "O", "O", "X", "O", "X", "O", ""]
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-9"
    Then the announcer section should display "Player X Won"
    And the announcer section should not have the class "hide"
    And all tiles on the game board should no longer accept clicks

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Game ends in a tie and displays the "Tie" message
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display tie message and disable further interactions when the game ends in a tie
  The system must detect when all tiles are filled without a winner, display a "Tie" message in the announcer section, and prevent further interactions with the game board.


Scenario: [Normal] Game ends in a tie and displays the "Tie" message
  Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
  And the board state is ["X", "O", "X", "X", "X", "O", "O", "", "O"]
  And it is player X's turn
  When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-8"
  Then the announcer section should display "Tie"
  And the announcer section should not have the class "hide"
  And all tiles on the game board should no longer accept clicks

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player X makes a valid move, and the turn switches to Player O
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Switch Current Player After a Valid Move
  The system must switch the current player and update the player display to indicate whose turn it is after a valid move.


  Scenario: [Normal] Player X makes a valid move, and the turn switches to Player O
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the current player display shows "Player X's turn" with data-testid "current-player"
    And the game board is empty
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-1"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-1" should display "X"
    And the current player display should update to "Player O's turn" with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Player O makes a valid move, and the turn switches to Player X
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Switch Current Player After a Valid Move
  The system must switch the current player and update the player display to indicate whose turn it is after a valid move.


Scenario: [Normal] Player O makes a valid move, and the turn switches to Player X
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And the tile with data-testid "tile-1" displays "X"
    And the current player display shows "Player O's turn" with data-testid "current-player"  
    When the user clicks on the tile with data-testid "tile-2"
    Then the tile with data-testid "tile-2" should display "O"
    And the current player display should update to "Player X's turn" with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Reset the game when the current player is 'X'
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Resetting the Tic Tac Toe game
  The reset button must clear all tiles, reset the internal game board state, hide the announcer section, and set the current player to 'X' if it was previously 'O'.


Scenario: [Normal] Reset the game when the current player is 'X'
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    And some tiles have been marked (e.g., tile with data-testid "tile-1" contains "X" and tile with data-testid "tile-2" contains "O")
    When the user clicks the reset button with data-testid "reset-button"
    Then all tiles (e.g., elements with data-testid "tile-1" to "tile-2”) should be empty
    And the current player should remain "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Reset the game when the current player is 'O'
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Resetting the Tic Tac Toe game
  The reset button must clear all tiles, reset the internal game board state, hide the announcer section, and set the current player to 'X' if it was previously 'O'.


Scenario: [Normal] Reset the game when the current player is 'O'
  Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
  And some tiles have been marked (e.g., the tile with data-testid "tile-4" contains "X")
  And the current player is displayed as "O" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
  When the user clicks the reset button with data-testid "reset-button"
  Then all tiles should be empty
  And the current player should be set to "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Reset the game after a win has been announced
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Resetting the Tic Tac Toe game
  The reset button must clear all tiles, reset the internal game board state, hide the announcer section, and set the current player to 'X' if it was previously 'O'.


Scenario: [Edge] Reset the game after a win has been announced
  Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
  And the board state is ["X", "X", "O", "O", "X", "O", "X", "O", "X"]
  And the announcer section with data-testid "announcer" displays "Player X Won"
  When the user clicks the reset button with data-testid "reset-button"
  Then all tiles (e.g., elements with data-testid "tile-1" to "tile-9") should be empty
  And the announcer section with data-testid "announcer" should be hidden
  And the current player should remain "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Reset the game after a tie has been announced
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Resetting the Tic Tac Toe game
  The reset button must clear all tiles, reset the internal game board state, hide the announcer section, and set the current player to 'X' if it was previously 'O'.


Scenario: [Edge] Reset the game after a tie has been announced
  Given the Tic Tac Toe game page is loaded
  And the board state is ["X", "X", "O", "O", "X", "X", "X", "O", "O"]
  And the announcer section with data-testid "announcer" displays "Tie"
  When the user clicks the reset button with data-testid "reset-button"
  Then all tiles (e.g., elements with data-testid "tile-1" to "tile-9") should be empty
  And the announcer section with data-testid "announcer" should be hidden
  And the current player should be set to "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"

reference_cases.title: [Error] Reset the game when no tiles have been marked
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Resetting the Tic Tac Toe game
  The reset button must clear all tiles, reset the internal game board state, hide the announcer section, and set the current player to 'X' if it was previously 'O'.


Scenario: [Error] Reset the game when no tiles have been marked
    Given the Tic Tac Toe game is loaded
    When the user clicks the reset button with data-testid "reset-button"
    Then all tiles (e.g., elements with data-testid "tile-1" to "tile-9") should remain empty
    And the internal game board state should remain reset to all empty values
    And the announcer section with data-testid "announcer" should remain hidden
    And the current player should remain "X" in the element with data-testid "current-player"
